pages.text: The **War Room Display** puts a launch network's whole picture up on a wall for the room: a screen seven blocks wide that everyone within 64 blocks of it sees. On it, the ground round the network and every member (the launchers numbered, with their aim; the radars with their reach; [Seismographs](ordnance/seismograph); the [Dead Hand](ordnance/dead_hand) and its radius); every missile the network's launchers fired (amber) and every one its radars track (red, with where it will come down); impacts; the blasts its seismographs felt; laser spots; the counts along the top and the network's last four reports along the bottom.

Seven wide and five high, one block deep: build it against a wall. The bottom row: Machine Casing, the controller in the middle and an Energy Port two to its right as you face it. Three rows of seven Display Panels above it, and a row of Machine Casing on top.

**Its header** has a clock (the world's time of day), its name plate and five lamps: the **alert condition**. 5 NORMAL; 4 ARMED (a launcher armed); 3 MISSILES IN FLIGHT (yours); 2 INCOMING (a missile its radars track coming down within 512 blocks of the network); 1 ATTACK (a blast felt within 512 blocks of it lately, or its Dead Hand in alert). The lamps flash at 2 and 1, and each new contact sounds its tone.

**Linking.** Use Launch Codes on it (the controller or any panel) to show their network; sneak while you use them to show none. It only shows the network and is no member of it, so any number of displays can show one network. Click the controller to set its view: everything fitted in, or centred on it at a scale (2 to 64 blocks a dot); and what it draws: the terrain, the radars' reach, labels, the log, blasts and impacts.

It needs 60 FE a tick; with no power, or in an EMP, it goes dark.
